The DXGW is a distributed set of BGP\\\\r\\\\nroute reflectors outside the data path: it selects the best VIF per prefix and reflects it, so a TGW\\\\r\\\\nor Cloud WAN CNE sees the DXGW as (usually) a single next hop and traffic goes straight to that VIF.\\\\r\\\\nThere is no second packet lookup at the DXGW.\\\\r\\\\n\\\\r\\\\n### ECMP is an outcome, not a step\\\\r\\\\nLongest prefix match comes first (a route lookup, not a BGP attribute). These BGP attributes are\\\\r\\\\nset at the VIF level on the on-prem router\\'s advertisements and evaluated by the DXGW. DXGW prefers\\\\r\\\\nthe local associated-region DX by default. Some DX locations serve more than one Region by port\\\\r\\\\nspeed, so check the associated Region of the specific connection, not just the location.\\\\r\\\\n\\\\r\\\\n### Transit Gateway with Direct Connect\\\\r\\\\nUse one DXGW with multiple transit VIFs for ECMP. BGP attributes stay on the VIFs and do not pass to\\\\r\\\\nthe TGW. Use multiple DXGWs only for traffic isolation or multiple primary paths. Across DXGWs on a\\\\r\\\\nTGW with no LP community and equal AS_PATH/MED, a local associated-Region DX wins on local\\\\r\\\\npreference over a remote one (no ECMP), and ECMP also needs matching DXGW Amazon-side ASNs. ## Relevant snippets

**Why aggregate prefixes may leave the local region:**
"If the region has no local DX advertisement (or a community forces a remote DX to win), the selected path points out of region, and traffic leaves the local region for egress — potentially bypassing local firewall inspection"

"For a region that has a **local** DX advertisement, the DXGW picks that local path on LP — AS-path (and therefore any prepend) is never consulted. So prepending a local VIF does **not** move that region's traffic off its local DX."

**DXGW local-region preference / associated-region behavior:**
"AWS applies a higher local preference to the path through a DX VIF in the same associated Region as the CNE. Local preference is compared before AS_PATH, and BGP stops at the first attribute that differs, so AS-path prepending cannot override it."

"Always check the associated Region of the specific DX *connection*; do not assume one Region per location."

"AWS sets the default LP per Region to prefer same-associated-Region DX (`7224:7200` medium) and sets it lower for others, unless LP communities are tagged."

**DXGW selection order (Lookup 1):**
"1. **Local-region Local Preference first** — if a DX VIF advertising the prefix is in the same associated region as the CNE, the DXGW prefers it **regardless of AS-path**. That local path is what the DXGW reflects to that region's CNE. 2. **If no local advertisement exists for that CNE**, every candidate is remote, so they share the **same (remote) LP** — LP is equal. The DXGW then falls through to **AS-path length**, and the **shortest AS-path wins**"

**Cloud WAN CNE route evaluation order (Lookup 2):**
"1. **Most specific route** (longest prefix match) — absolute, wins before everything. 2. For same-destination routes with different targets: 1. Static routes 2. System routes (1:1 NAT) 3. VPC-propagated routes (same region) 4. **Dynamic routes, compared in order** — selection stops at the first attribute that differs: 1. **Local preference** set by a Cloud WAN routing policy (`set-local-preference`) — higher wins; the default is 0. 2. **AS-path length** — shortest wins 3. **MED** — lowest wins"

**Longest-prefix-match implications with aggregate vs. more-specific:**
"Step 1 (longest prefix match) is absolute — each CNE route table forwards to the correct DX based on destination address."

"**Pattern 3: Per-Region Control via More Specific Routes** — Advertise more-specific prefixes from the corresponding DX location… **Result:** Step 1 (longest prefix match) is absolute — each CNE route table forwards to the correct DX based on destination address."

"Worked Example… **Only **FR5/Frankfurt (eu-central-1)** and **LD5/Slough** advertise `11.0.0.0/8`**" [table showing that eu-central-1 with local FR5 wins on LP before AS-path, eu-west-1 with local LD5 wins on LP, while regions without local `/8` fall to AS-path tiebreak where FR5 wins]

**LP communities (`7224:7300/7200/7100`) — steering mechanisms:**
"**Explicit LP communities override DXGW's default local-region preference** — applying `7224:7300/7200/7100` on advertised prefixes forces DXGW to honor the explicit LP before applying its local-vs-remote default."

"**LP communities are evaluated before AS-path** — per DX documentation: 'Local preference BGP community tags are evaluated before any AS_PATH attribute.' This applies at the DXGW path selection stage."

"**Always use LP communities (`7224:7300/7200/7100`) for expected egress routing** — High Preference BGP communities are the recommended mechanism to achieve predictable DX egress behavior."

"| DX Location | Community | Role | |---|---|---| | Primary DX location | `7224:7300` | HIGH — globally preferred | | Secondary DX location | `7224:7200` | MEDIUM — failover | | All other DX locations | `7224:7100` | LOW — last resort |"

**Set-local-preference in Cloud WAN routing policies:**
"**Routing policies on the native Cloud WAN DXGW attachment** (filtering, summarization, path preferences) — Cloud WAN Routing Policies (core network policy version **2025.11 or later**) support, on Direct Connect attachments: … **path preferences** — setting **local preference, AS_PATH or MED** on inbound and outbound route propagations."

"**Primary lever — Cloud WAN routing policies** (policy version 2025.11 or later): apply an **inbound** routing policy to each DXGW attachment that sets **local preference** (or AS_PATH / MED) for the matching prefixes or prefix lists"

"A higher local preference is preferred; the default is 0."

**AS-path prepend/remove/replace in Cloud WAN routing policies:**
"actions include `allow`/`drop` (terminal), `set-local-preference` and `set-med` (non-terminal), the AS_PATH actions `prepend-asn-list`, `remove-asn-list` and `replace-asn-list`"

"`replace-asn-list` is not supported cross-Region (CNE-to-CNE)."

**AS-path prepending pitfall:**
"**Common Pitfall: AS-Path Prepending Does Not Override Local-Region LP at the DXGW** — **The mistaken assumption:** 'If I prepend a DX VIF's prefix enough, I can steer that region's traffic away from (or toward) it across regions.' **Why it's wrong:** DX egress selection happens at the **DXGW lookup** (see 'Two Route Lookups' below), where **local-region Local Preference is evaluated before AS-path**. For a region that has a **local** DX advertisement, the DXGW picks that local path on LP — AS-path (and therefore any prepend) is never consulted."

"**To steer cross-region DX preference, use LP communities (which are evaluated before AS-path at the DXGW), not prepending.**"

{"id": "d045252c-ce4d-4d44-b217-b7d6053db880", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's how Cloud WAN decides this, and the levers to fix it.

## Two separate route lookups happen

**Lookup 1 — DXGW selects a path per prefix** (happens before Cloud WAN sees anything):
- If a DX VIF in the **same associated Region as the CNE** advertises the prefix, the DXGW always prefers it on local-region **local preference** — **before AS-path is even consulted**. AS-path prepending cannot override this.
- If there's **no local advertisement** for that CNE's region, every candidate is remote, LP is equal across them, and the DXGW falls through to **shortest AS-path**, then MED.
- The DXGW then reflects a single best path to each region's Core Network Edge (CNE) — Cloud WAN doesn't see the candidates it rejected.

**Lookup 2 — the CNE's own route table evaluation** (per the [Cloud WAN route evaluation docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-route-evaluation.html)):
1. Longest prefix match — absolute, wins before anything else
2. Static → system (1:1 NAT) → VPC-propagated (same region)
3. Dynamic routes, first difference wins: local preference (set by a Cloud WAN routing policy, default 0) → AS-path length → MED
4. If still tied: source preference (DXGW-propagated > Connect > VPN > other), or deterministically random if truly equal

## Why your aggregate is leaving the region

Two likely causes:
- **No local DX advertisement of that aggregate.** If the local VIF only advertises more-specific prefixes (not the summarized/aggregate one), the DXGW has nothing local to prefer for that aggregate, falls to the remote-vs-remote AS-path tiebreak, and a remote DX wins — even though your local DX is up and healthy for everything else.
- **An LP community on a remote VIF is explicitly overriding the default.** `7224:7300` (High) on a remote advertisement beats the DXGW's implicit local-region preference, since LP communities are evaluated before AS-path and before the "local wins by default" rule.

Longest-prefix-match at the CNE (Lookup 2, step 1) is absolute, so if a more-specific route exists locally, it already wins regardless of this discussion — the aggregate-leaving-region symptom specifically points at the DXGW-level decision on that less-specific prefix.

## How to prefer the local DX

| Scenario | Fix |
|---|---|
| Local VIF doesn't advertise the aggregate at all | Advertise the aggregate (not just the more-specifics) from the local on-prem router |
| A remote VIF is tagged with a higher LP community | Lower it, or tag the local VIF with `7224:7300` (High) / `7224:7200` (Medium) so it wins explicitly — don't rely on prepending, it's ignored once a local advertisement exists |
| Multiple DXGWs feed the same CNE | DX LP communities can't be matched/set on Cloud WAN DX attachments directly — instead apply an **inbound Cloud WAN routing policy** on the DXGW attachment with `set-local-preference` for the prefix (requires core network policy version **2025.11+**); `prepend-asn-list`/`remove-asn-list`/`set-med` are also available but LP is the cleanest lever here |
| Want deterministic per-region control generally | Advertise more-specific prefixes per region — longest-prefix-match is absolute and bypasses all of this |

Note: AS-path prepending only reliably works for choosing between **same-region** VIFs. For cross-region steering, local-region LP at the DXGW overrides it every time.

## Validation (read-only)

- `aws directconnect describe-connections` — confirm which associated Region each physical connection/VIF actually maps to (some locations serve more than one Region)
- `aws directconnect list-virtual-interface-routes --virtual-interface-id <vif-id>` — see the exact AS-path and communities AWS received for that VIF
- Compare the Cloud WAN console's **Route information base** (pre-policy) against **Routes** (installed) tabs to see whether a routing policy is changing the outcome
- `get-network-routes` for the CNE to confirm what's actually installed

I'd recommend testing any community or policy change in non-production first, since it affects path selection for every region sharing that DXGW. If you want, I can pull your actual DX connections and VIF advertisements to check which one of these is happening in your account.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
